title: 5 people. 4 months. 11 hours of cinematic story. Here’s how we used AI to finish it.
author: Proper_Implement_394

comments.author: pickleunicorn
comments.body:
Well, sadly, what lost me is... The AI. The fact I can see it proves that this is not as good as an "Unreal Engine" cinematic, which, as a gamer, is what I'm used to.

Other than that, what's the game? What's the gameplay? Because having a great gameplay, a great story is more important than dealing with not visually "perfect" cinematics.

replies.author: Proper_Implement_394
replies.body:
That’s fair. If the visible AI artifacts break the experience for you, I understand.

The game is a choice-driven cinematic narrative rather than a traditional action game. Your decisions affect relationships, character survival, different timelines, and multiple endings. This trailer leaned too heavily on atmosphere and didn’t show that gameplay loop clearly enough. Our next cut needs to include an actual decision and its consequence.

replies.author: pickleunicorn
replies.body: That would be interesting yes ! Also, comments can be harsh but the more important is really the scenario itself. If it's good, then the imperfections won't matter that much ;)

comments.author: duffpl
comments.body: What's the point of creating cinematics without showing any gameplay or what the game is? This just looks like mashup of AI generated videos. Some characters look like CGI, some are real, there is just lots of VFX and these screens with questions/bulletpoints look pretty bad. All is kind of soulless and lacks art direction. Or is the game just bunch of AI videos where you branch off based on your decision? e.g. if I choose A then video #125 plays and then if I choose B then video #531 plays?

replies.author: strenghtineer
replies.body: And this is exactly why most heavily AI-generated content is going to fail. The people making it simply don’t have the eye to tell when the generated content actually looks good and when it looks genuinely distracting and painfully AI-generated.

replies.author: Proper_Implement_394
replies.body:
That’s fair. At its core, this is a choice-driven cinematic narrative rather than a traditional action game: you watch scenes, make decisions, and those decisions affect relationships, who survives, which timeline you enter, and which ending you reach.

So your basic read of the structure isn’t entirely wrong—but this trailer should have shown an actual choice and its consequence instead of expecting viewers to infer the gameplay from a montage. The comments about the mixed visual styles and UI screens are useful too.

Would seeing a choice and its immediate consequence within the first 20 seconds make the format clearer, or would you rather see a longer uninterrupted gameplay sequence?

comments.author: Chaoppa
comments.body: Trailer is very cool but from a gamer’s perspective I see all kinds of completely different scenes stitched together that I fail to connect in a coherent way of what this game is about.

comments.author: ChirpXel
comments.body:
Congrats on the success on your game! This type of trailer might work more for an Asian market. But personally, it feels a bit too generic AI feel for me.   
I do think AI is an important tool for the future of game development, but it does have a genric look that should be avoided. We are still artists / creators we should push the look AS MUCH as possible always

replies.author: Proper_Implement_394
replies.body:
Thank you—this is fair. AI made it possible for a five-person team to build something at this scale, but “made with AI” can’t be the visual identity of the game.

If the trailer still reads as generic AI, then we haven’t pushed the art direction and visual consistency far enough. We’re taking that seriously for the next cut, along with showing the actual choice-driven gameplay much earlier.

Was there a particular shot where that generic AI feeling became most obvious to you?

comments.author: EmotionalFan5429
comments.body:
\- No gameplay shown  
\- Generic ChatGPT images as first frames  
\- Mix of art styles  
\- Close ups of ugly zombie faces, that try to scare by coming even closer  
\- Chinese language  
\- Generic screaming female characters

replies.author: Proper_Implement_394
replies.body:
Thanks for being direct. The lack of visible gameplay and the mixed visual styles are fair criticisms.

The game is a choice-driven cinematic narrative, but because this cut never shows a decision or its consequence, it ends up reading as a montage rather than a game trailer. That’s the clearest thing we need to fix in the next version.

replies.author: pickleunicorn
replies.body: Well, it's not necessarily targeted to the rest of the world. China is already a big market and if you want to create a narrative game, it's better to do it in your own language than failing to translate it well.

comments.author: excellentforcongress
comments.body:
people are being haters.

i don't really agree with excessive use of purely ai generated video because it is on the higher end of computational intensity and the environmental issues involved but from a cinema perspective this is better than a lot of other shitty trailers.

replies.author: Proper_Implement_394
replies.body:
I appreciate that. And the concern about computational and environmental cost is fair—it isn’t something we should treat casually.

The criticism here is still useful, especially the repeated point that we didn’t show the actual interaction clearly enough. The next trailer needs to prove what the player does, not just show how much content we made.

replies.author: excellentforcongress
replies.body:
yes i think an honest trailer would do you well, i looked at the reviews and they seem split between people who liked the game, and people who didn't know the game was not very game-y

it seems more like interactive cinema
